page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, providing a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core ratio with 1.0 thread per core. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it lacks GPU hardware. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Geekbench text processing also demonstrates strong results. However, multi-core performance is average, as shown by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff: while large-block write bandwidth is average, read-only memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks falls into the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are weak, scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c8a.xlarge offers a dedicated AMD EPYC compute profile with a low RAM-to-vCPU ratio, making it a resource-dense option for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. Due to its weak database and memory read performance, it is less suitable for memory-cached databases or high-throughput web serving. It is best aligned with single-threaded compute workloads, basic text processing, and lightweight multi-core processing tasks that fit within its 8.0 GB memory limit.
